lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Date of birth is unnecessary and should be removed.
items.because: It can create age-discrimination concerns and does not help establish qualification.

items.says: Nationality should be removed unless specifically required.
items.because: It is normally omitted and work eligibility should be stated only if relevant.

items.says: Add a clear target-role headline or summary at the top.
items.because: A recruiter has to infer your intended role; the resume should make it obvious immediately.

items.says: Check the portfolio link for completeness and relevance.
items.because: It should contain the listed projects, readable documentation, and demonstrate the engineering decisions implied by the resume.

items.says: Clarify that the M.S. degree is in progress.
items.because: Employers distinguish between completed and in-progress degrees.

items.says: Check that institution names, locations, and degree names are accurate and consistently formatted.
items.because: If anonymized, replace with real names before applying.

items.says: Clarify what 'diagnostic accuracy' means.
items.because: The metric is not self-explanatory and could refer to several different measures.

items.says: Clarify the baseline for the 35% improvement.
items.because: The result is more credible if the comparison point is clear.

items.says: Explain 'validated tool-use trajectories' in more accessible terms.
items.because: Not all readers will understand this technical phrase.

items.says: Explain the 'reviewer disagreement' metric more clearly.
items.because: It could be interpreted several ways and needs context.

items.says: Clarify your ownership of the routing layer design.
items.because: Be precise about which parts you designed, implemented, evaluated, and deployed.

items.says: Avoid overloading the bullet with too many details in one sentence.
items.because: It is dense and may require rereading to understand.

items.says: Make the evaluation condition 'at equal accuracy' prominent.
items.because: It prevents the reader from assuming quality was sacrificed for efficiency.

items.says: Clarify your role in the GRPO training and reward design.
items.because: Be precise about your ownership and avoid overstating your contribution.

items.says: Clarify whether a 5% latency reduction is operationally significant.
items.because: It may be less impressive unless the baseline or impact is explained.

items.says: Move the evaluation harness bullet earlier in the section.
items.because: Evaluation is a central theme and should be more prominent.

items.says: Clarify what 'citation quality' measured.
items.because: The term is broad and could mean several things.

items.says: Specify whether the evaluation harness was adopted as a standard process.
items.because: It would be stronger if it became part of a release or CI workflow.

items.says: Remove or merge this bullet as it duplicates the first bullet's technical mechanism.
items.because: Repetition makes the section look less substantial and wastes space.

items.says: Do not present the same accomplishment twice.
items.because: The first bullet covers the outcome; this one covers the method.

items.says: Review the causal claim about assistant-only loss masking improving faithfulness.
items.because: It may overstate what the method alone accomplished.

items.says: Move this bullet to the top of the experience section.
items.because: It has the clearest production impact and communicates scale and business value.

items.says: Clarify your relationship to the launch and the backlog reduction.
items.because: The reader should know your role in building, deploying, or analyzing the impact.

items.says: Remove this duplicated triage bullet from the project section.
items.because: It is almost identical to the Mobility Systems Company bullet and may be seen as padding or a copy-paste error.

items.says: Explain the business meaning of the 'pending-case backlog'.
items.because: It is operationally vague and the reader should know its impact.

items.says: Clarify what 'GPU memory' refers to (peak, per-device, etc.).
items.because: A technical reviewer will want to understand the measurement.

items.says: Add the operational consequence of the memory reduction if available.
items.because: It would be more valuable if it enabled larger models, batch sizes, or cost savings.

items.says: Be prepared to explain the technical appropriateness of BF16.
items.because: The claim invites technical follow-up on hardware support and stability.

items.says: Clarify what the p95 latency measurement covers.
items.because: The reader should know if it is end-to-end, API layer, or specific operation.

items.says: Correct the tense and subject agreement in this bullet.
items.because: It shifts from past tense to a singular present-tense verb, which is a grammar error.

items.says: Clarify the result 'shortened release cycles to 3 days'.
items.because: It is unclear whether releases took three days before, after, or were reduced by three days.

items.says: Explain what the automated regression checks covered.
items.because: Specify which type of regression was prevented or detected.

items.says: Check for overlap with the evaluation harness bullet.
items.because: Both involve automated evaluation and release protection; each should have a distinct scope.

items.says: Clarify the scale or service impact of migrating 30 robot-fleet services.
items.because: Add throughput, failure rate, dispatch impact, or operational frequency if available.

items.says: Explain your role in the migration.
items.because: 'Migrated' can imply full ownership; clarify architecture, implementation, rollout, and coordination.

items.says: Clarify what 'morning dispatch' refers to in business terms.
items.because: The business context determines how impressive the result appears.

items.says: Replace the vague 'AI-first engineering practices' bullet with a concrete, measurable technical contribution.
items.because: It is a generic claim with no baseline, scale, artifact, or measurable result.

items.says: Clarify what you personally built in the project.
items.because: The bullet describes broad influence rather than implementation.

items.says: Add evidence of adoption only if it is real and quantifiable.
items.because: If downstream teams used the runtime, quantify users or deployments.

items.says: Clarify the measurement setup for context management.
items.because: A reviewer will want to know what counted as working context and how quality was preserved.

items.says: Add a quality or reliability outcome if available.
items.because: Token reduction alone may be interpreted as information loss.

items.says: Explain the relevance of the 100-turn stress test.
items.because: The reader should know why it reflects a realistic workload.

items.says: Clarify the previous failure mode for deadlocks and lost tool results.
items.because: The reviewer needs to know if these were observed bugs, test failures, or risks.

items.says: Explain the significance of 50-way fan-out.
items.because: The scale should connect to expected workload or stress-test design.

items.says: Distinguish removal of deadlocks from prevention.
items.because: 'Removing' suggests the issue no longer occurs; ensure evidence supports this.

items.says: Clarify whether you selected, implemented, or integrated the eight metrics.
items.because: A reviewer may want to know the nature of your contribution.

items.says: Identify the evaluation dimensions covered by the metrics.
items.because: Clarify what kinds of research-agent behavior the framework evaluates.

items.says: Explain what the Kendall correlation means and what it is measured against.
items.because: A reader may not know if it is against degradation, human judgment, or another reference.

items.says: Clarify the degradation protocol used in the evaluation.
items.because: The reviewer should know if it was controlled, random, staged, or manual.

items.says: Avoid implying broad validity from one correlation result.
items.because: It shows sensitivity to the tested degradation, not general evaluator validity.

items.says: Remove this duplicated triage bullet unless it genuinely belongs to the project.
items.because: It is almost identical to the Mobility Systems Company bullet and may confuse chronology and ownership.

items.says: Expand the skills section to reflect demonstrated ML systems and evaluation work.
items.because: The experience shows much more than the skills section acknowledges.

items.says: Add technologies clearly demonstrated in the resume, such as mixed-precision training, distributed systems, event-driven architecture, model evaluation, tool-use training, inference optimization, caching, CI/CD, statistical evaluation, and open-source contribution.
items.because: These should be represented if they are genuine skills.

items.says: Clarify what 'agent evaluation' means in the skills section.
items.because: It is broad and could refer to several types of evaluation.

items.says: Remove low-signal entries like Git if space is limited.
items.because: Git is nearly universal and contributes little by itself.

items.says: Reorder bullets within Mobility Systems Company to prioritize production impact and system architecture.
items.because: The current order postpones the clearest production outcome.

items.says: Reorder bullets within Eastern Robotics Co. based on the target role.
items.because: The ordering should reflect the job being targeted, not just chronology.

items.says: Separate research-engineering and production-engineering narratives or connect them with a consistent theme.
items.because: Otherwise, the resume may appear unfocused.

items.says: Make the projects section support the experience section without duplicating achievements or using weaker claims.
items.because: Projects should demonstrate independent depth or open-source contribution.

items.says: Fix line wrapping and formatting issues.
items.because: Poor wrapping makes the document look less polished.

items.says: Correct grammar and tense consistency throughout the resume.
items.because: Grammar errors undermine professional credibility.

items.says: Standardize technical terminology (e.g., tool-use, multi-agent, fine-tuning, end-to-end, dead-letter, p95, BF16).
items.because: Inconsistent styling makes the resume look assembled from different drafts.

items.says: Check if the resume is too dense and remove duplicated or generic material before reducing font size.
items.because: The technical detail could become difficult to scan.
